summary: Admit a bounded, idempotent Telegram webhook subscription lifecycle through the tenant-scoped host API.

impacts.evidence: The protected route resolves the social account inside the authenticated organization/workspace scope before provider egress.
Bot credentials and callback secret stay in SecretProvider; operation and audit records contain no provider secret or raw response.
OpenAPI adds authenticated subscribe and unsubscribe operations with bounded input and replay responses.
Subscription lifecycle emits no new domain event and reuses the existing inbound webhook bridge.
SocialWebhookController is an additive provider-neutral SDK surface resolved only by qualified built-in runtime composition.
The existing tenant-scoped operation receipt stores the normalized lifecycle result.
Authentication, tenant binding, capability, HTTPS endpoint bounds, callback-scoped secret use and exact endpoint delete guard are independent gates.
The protected account configuration mutation requires connectors.accounts.write and is recorded as write-sensitive audit evidence.
Subscribe and unsubscribe capture an immutable action with idempotency correlation and account resource identity.
Completed operation receipts replay without a provider call; pending and ambiguous provider outcomes are not retried automatically.
The adapter uses the official Telegram lifecycle API, bounded endpoint validation and no caller-controlled provider destination beyond the requested deployment endpoint.
Provider failures map to bounded API errors and audit entries are written only after confirmed lifecycle completion.
Capability removal closes admission; unsubscribe is guarded by the provider-reported endpoint and does not rewrite inbound evidence.
Deterministic connector, runtime, API, OpenAPI, SDK and repository checks cover success, replay, provider failure and endpoint mismatch.
